title: 2014 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: A set \(S\) consists of triangles whose sides have integer lengths less than \(5,\) and no two elements of \(S\) are congruent or similar. What is the largest number of elements that \(S\) can have?

solutions.text:
Write each triangle by its side lengths in nonincreasing order. Only one equilateral triangle is allowed (all are similar), and of the similar pair \(2,2,1\) and \(4,4,2\) only one may appear.

The remaining valid, pairwise non-similar triangles are \[ \begin{gathered} 4\,4\,3,\ 4\,4\,1,\ 4\,3\,3,\ 4\,3\,2,\ \\ 3\,3\,2,\ 3\,3\,1,\ 3\,2\,2, \end{gathered} \] seven in all. Together with one equilateral and one of the similar pair, \(S\) has at most \(9\) elements.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: List each triangle by its sides in nonincreasing order using values from \(\{1,2,3,4\}\)
Drop those failing the triangle inequality, and count \(2,2,1\) and \(4,4,2\) only once since they are similar
